text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Moslem chairman of three-men Bosnian Presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, summoned diplomats from international Contact Group to discuss issue of disputed northern town of Brcko.

- "I don't believe the international community would dare to, by giving Brcko to the Serbs, turns its eyes from the basic standards of civilisation and put the peace process under a question mark, knowing that genocide of the worst kind happened there," says Haris Silajdzic, Moslem co-chairman in the Bosnian Council of Ministers.
- "Until someone states publicly that Brcko will belong to the Serbs I don't believe it may happen," adviser to chairman of the collective Bosnian Presidency, Mirza Hajric, says.
- International peace envoy Carl Bildt opens regional office in divided Bosnian town of Mostar which will be headed by British diplomat Sir Martin Garrod.
- Government agency for employment says 176,918 unemployed were registered in Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation as of December 31, 1996.
- National Bank of Bosnia offers 20 million German marks for sale to commercial banks in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
- The Moslem-Croat Federation Army will be organised to suit NATO standards and its Partnership for Peace programme, a deputy of Federation Defence Minister says in interview.

- Chief of international High Representative office in Mostar, Sir Martin Garrod, urges senior Croat official to stop illegal construction of a Croat national theater in the central part of divided town.
